tested_semantics: unrelated state change does not force an effect-precondition abort
relevant dependency version change blocks handoff to runtime authority
a dependency absent from the cognitive snapshot requires re-assembly
guard hashing is deterministic under dependency-order permutation
commit epoch cannot precede snapshot epoch
the commit guard itself always has authority NONE

sqlite_runtime_probe.interpretation: A cognition-phase read snapshot must not be assumed safely upgradeable into the later effect write transaction after concurrent state change. Close/materialize cognition, then start a fresh commit transaction and revalidate effect-relevant state.

dependency_revalidation_proxy.interpretation: In this constructed uniform-key workload, rejecting every effect whenever any global state changed creates large false-abort pressure. Revalidating only the declared effect-relevant dependency closure preserves the stale-effect protection of checking relevant dependencies while allowing unrelated state changes. This is a mechanism sanity check, not a calibrated FRANK workload estimate.

negative_results_and_limits: No Andreas-PC target-Ubuntu execution was performed.
The synthetic key-change workload is deliberately simple and does not estimate real FRANK update distributions.
This experiment does not prove that dependency-closure revalidation is sufficient when dependencies are incomplete or dynamically discovered.
Dependency laundering is therefore fail-closed: a newly required dependency absent from the cognitive snapshot forces re-assembly.
The guard does not execute effects and does not replace the runtime-minted opaque capability boundary.
